title: Quiche au Saumon
subtitle: Smoked salmon and dill quiche
excerpt: Quiche au saumon is a French tart filled with smoked salmon, crème fraîche, dill, and eggs. The filling is richer and creamier than quiche Lorraine, with the salmon providing salt and the dill cutting through the fat. It is served at room temperature, making it good for buffets and lunches.
sourceNotes: A modern French tart using smoked salmon, a combination that became popular in French home cooking from the 1970s onward as refrigerated smoked salmon became widely available.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before and refrigerate. Serve at room temperature.

content.text: The combination of smoked salmon and crème fraîche makes a filling that is richer than a classic Lorraine. The salmon provides enough salt that you will need very little additional seasoning. Do not add smoked salmon before baking: it goes rubbery. Lay it over the filling once the custard has partially set, about 20 minutes into the bake.

Roll the pastry to 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line with baking parchment and baking beans and blind-bake for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and paper and bake for 5 minutes more until the base is dry. Reduce the oven to 180°C fan.

Whisk together the eggs, crème fraîche, double cream, dill, and lemon zest. Season with black pepper: go very easy on the salt as the salmon is already salty. Pour the custard into the blind-baked pastry case.

Bake for 20 minutes. The custard will be partially set around the edges but still liquid in the centre. Open the oven, lay the smoked salmon slices over the surface, and return to the oven for a further 15 to 20 minutes until the custard is fully set with a slight wobble in the centre. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: Smoked salmon has gone rubbery and overcooked
items.cause: Salmon was added at the start with the custard and cooked for the full time
items.fix: Always add smoked salmon halfway through baking when the custard is partially set, never at the beginning.

items.cause: Salt added without accounting for the salt already in the smoked salmon
items.fix: Taste the custard mixture before adding any salt. With good smoked salmon you may need none.

content.text: Serve at room temperature rather than hot: the flavour of smoked salmon is better when it is not piping hot. This is a good buffet dish for the same reason. A simple green salad with a lemon vinaigrette alongside is the natural pairing.
